program: [ quote [ cons ] cat ] map [ [ quote cat ] cat ] map swap [ quote ] map [ [ uncons ] dip i ] fold [ uncons quote eq? ] filter [ uncons swap drop ] map
notes: Turn each y into the 4-atom action (y cons quote cat) and each x into (x); a rotation fold [ [ uncons ] dip i ] pops the next (x), runs the y action on it and appends the pair (y x); then filter pairs by [ uncons quote eq? ] and map to the head. Each quotation run by i is data-built and also 4 atoms.

program: [ quote [ cons ] cat ] map [ [ quote cat ] cat ] map nil quote nil cons [ [ uncons ] dip i ] fold uncons swap uncons swap drop [ quote [ add ] cat ] map [ [ quote cat ] cat ] map swap [ [ uncons ] dip i ] fold nil [ cons ] fold [ 1 1 add div ] map
notes: Split into reversed evens and odds: build the actions (x cons quote cat) and rotation-fold them over (nil nil). Unpack at top level, turn the odds into (o add quote cat) and rotation-fold them over the evens to get pair sums. Then reverse and map [ 1 1 add div ]. The rotation driver [ [ uncons ] dip i ] is 4 atoms, and so is every action it runs.

program: dup uncons drop uncons drop [ quote [ sub ] cat ] map [ [ quote cat ] cat ] map swap [ [ uncons ] dip i ] fold uncons drop uncons drop dup [ 0 swap sub ] map cat [ 0 swap lt? ] filter 0 [ add ] fold
notes: No point pairing needed: the length is the sum of |x[i] - x[i+2]|. A lag-2 rotation zip (xs[2:] as actions (x sub quote cat) over xs) builds the differences, and uncons drop uncons drop discards the two leftover heads. Absolute sum: cat the differences with their negations, filter the positives and fold with [ add ].
